newsitem.title: USA: Rexene seeks to block special meeting call.
newsitem.headline: Rexene seeks to block special meeting call.

text.p: Rexene Corp on Tuesday said it was seeking to block a solicitation for a special shareholder meeting called by Guy Wyser-Pratte and Spear, Leeds & Kellogg.
Wyser-Pratte, of Wyser-Pratte & Co, and Spear, Leeds & Kellogg last week called for the meeting. They have pressed for the company to be sold for $16 a share and want to install a new board.
Wyser-Pratte and Spear, Leeds & Kellogg own about 10.1 percent of Rexene's outstanding common stock.
Rexene said it began to mail a revocation solicitation statement to stockholders in opposition to the solicitation made by Wyser-Pratte and Spear, Leeds & Kellogg for a special meeting.
The Rexene board of directors opposes the Wyser-Pratte solicitation, which it describes as "a complete waste of time and money" in a statement.
The board said it "believes the Wyser-Pratte group proposes to do nothing that has not already been fully explored by Rexene's incumbent directors."
In a letter accompanying the statement, Chairman and Chief Executive Andrew Smith said, "The Wyser-Pratte group says they want to gain control of Rexene so they can attempt to sell the company.
He added, "... To date, no one -- including Huntsman Corp -- has made a suitable offer." Rexene has rejected an unsolicited $16-a-share cash offer from Huntsman.
Shares in Rexene, a maker of thermoplastic resins and petrochemical products, closed on Tuesday at 14.
